diagnosis.root_cause: A shared splitter or splitter-side distribution fault on EPON0/6 has taken multiple ONUs offline while other ONUs on the same PON remain online. Customer 22371 is one of the affected offline ONUs; its prior optical telemetry was stable and normal, so there is no evidence of individual fibre or laser degradation.
evidence: The live ONU probe definitively reports customer 22371 as offline: responds=true and online=0, with MPCP DEREG and Una uth status.
The EPON0/6 port probe shows five definite offline ONUs (indices 15, 16, 19, 20, and 46) while four peers (8, 13, 49, and 57) remain online.
Two or more offline ONUs with surviving peers places the failure boundary inside the PON port and identifies a splitter failure rather than a single ONU outage or whole-port failure.
The OLT responds to ping, SNMP, and the relevant OID subtree; OLT CPU, memory, temperature, and historical telemetry are normal, so this is not an OLT failure.
The router heartbeat is healthy and customer VLAN 1016 is present and correctly assigned, ruling out router reachability and VLAN 46 provisioning faults.

The customer's seven-day RX readings stayed around -22.3 to -23.1 dBm, within the normal band and without a decline; TX power remained near +2.3 dBm, TX bias remained healthy, and distance stayed constant at 294 m.
The customer's current zero optical readings mean no reading because the ONU is offline, not strong signal; the live offline result confirms the service fault.
The OLT-wide offline total of 25 is above the normal background estimate, but the direct port probe provides stronger evidence and localizes the outage to EPON0/6.
The customer has only one session in the last 24 hours with a normal long duration, so authentication flapping is not supported.

remediation.action: Dispatch field maintenance to inspect the EPON0/6 splitter and downstream distribution connections, including power, connectors, and fibre continuity; repair or replace the failed splitter/branch or restore the affected path. Verify that all affected ONUs re-register and that RX/TX readings return, then clear the mass-ONU-offline alarm.

ground_truth.root_cause: Eleven of the thirty-four customers on EPON0/6 lost service within the same minute while the remaining twenty-three continue normally. A shared downstream splitter branch has failed; the PON port itself is still working.
expected_reasoning: Probing EPON0/6 shows eleven ONUs offline and twenty-three still online with normal RX and TX
Because part of the port is still serving, the port optics and feeder fibre are working
The eleven failures occurred within the same minute, which rules out unrelated individual faults
A simultaneous partial loss on a working port indicates a shared element downstream of the port
That element is a splitter branch serving those eleven customers
OLT ping, SNMP, CPU, memory and temperature are all normal, so the OLT is not involved
The health check still reports the OLT healthy, which is correct here but only because the port has surviving ONUs
PON port traffic has fallen but not collapsed, consistent with losing a third of the port
The affected set is the eleven, not the whole port
distractors: Eleven simultaneous outages could be read as a PON port failure if the surviving ONUs are not probed
The OLT health check reports healthy, inviting a no_fault conclusion
The affected ONU indexes are not contiguous, obscuring the shared branch
